classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied sequence from Earth radius plus altitude to orbital circumference, then interpret one orbit as that distance in 24 hours and calculate speed.

content.prompt: A satellite has a circular orbit 800 km above the Earth’s surface.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the radius of the Earth is 6400 km, find the radius of the orbit of the satellite.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the circumference of the satellite’s orbit, to the nearest kilometre.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If the satellite makes one orbit in a day, find the speed of the satellite. Give your answer in km/h, to the nearest km/h.

answer.worked:
One day is 24 hours. Use the unrounded circumference.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{d}{t}\\s&=\frac{14\,400\pi}{24}\\s&=600\pi\text{ km/h}\\s&\approx1885\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$
